pull.title: KAFKA-21343: Route bootstrap DNS resolution through HostResolver
pull.body:
JIRA: KAFKA-21343 This PR aims to make async bootstrap dns mechanism
testable. It routes bootstrap resolution through HostResolver too, using
the same injection point already exposed by KafkaAdminClient.

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Bootstrap address construction can lose configured hostnames, and the integration test does not reliably detect bypassed bootstrap resolver injection.
2 open issues - [Preserve bootstrap hostname for unnamed resolved addresses](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23934#discussion_r4358864199) · New - [Ensure test fails when bootstrap resolver injection is bypassed](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23934#discussion_r4358864298) · New
What changed in this PR Routes asynchronous bootstrap DNS resolution through the existing `HostResolver` injection point, making bootstrap failures testable through `KafkaAdminClient`. **Changes:** - Adds resolver-aware address-parsing overloads and uses them for initial bootstrap resolution and retries. - Adds transient DNS failure recovery tests at the network-client and admin-client levels. - Disables bootstrap in existing connection tests to isolate resolver call counts. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `clients/​src/​test/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​clients/​NetworkClientTest.java` | Tests bootstrap DNS recovery and isolates existing connection tests. | | `clients/​src/​main/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​clients/​NetworkClient.java` | Passes the injected resolver to bootstrap resolution and retries. | | `clients/​src/​main/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​clients/​ClientUtils.java` | Adds resolver-aware parsing while retaining default-resolver overloads. | | `clients/​clients-integration-tests/​src/​test/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​clients/​admin/​AsyncBootstrapResolutionTest.java` | Adds admin-client recovery coverage for transient DNS failures. |
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟡 Changes recommended Failed DNS resolution can bypass port validation and silently accept an invalid bootstrap entry when another entry resolves.
1 open issue - [Validate port range before resolving hostnames](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23934#discussion_r4358982030) · New
2 resolved since last review - [Preserve bootstrap hostname for unnamed resolved addresses](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23934#discussion_r4358864199) - [Ensure test fails when bootstrap resolver injection is bypassed](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23934#discussion_r4358864298)
Review effort: Balanced

### 🔵 Needs a closer look Canonical-name bootstrap still bypasses the injected resolver for its forward lookup, leaving that path dependent on JVM DNS. **No open issues** 🎉
1 previously missed issue In code that hasn't changed since last review
Route canonical bootstrap forward lookups through the injected resolver `clients/​src/​main/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​clients/​ClientUtils.java:79` With `RESOLVE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_ONLY`, the injected resolver controls the initial lookup, but `new InetSocketAddress(resolvedCanonicalName, port)` still performs the canonical-name forward lookup through JVM DNS. An injected mapping for that canonical name is ignored; if JVM DNS cannot resolve it, the bootstrap address is discarded even when the injected resolver could resolve it. Route this forward lookup through `hostResolver` as well, preserving the canonical hostname and the existing behavior of skipping unresolved canonical names. Add an injected-resolver test for this mode so it does not rely on real DNS for the forward lookup.
1 resolved since last review - [Validate port range before resolving hostnames](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23934#discussion_r4358982030)
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: When the injected resolver returns an unnamed InetAddress, such as one created from an IP literal, this constructor drops the configured bootstrap hostname. Cluster.bootstrap() copies the socket's getHostString() into Node.host(), and ClusterConnectionStates later resolves that value again. A resolver keyed by the bootstrap hostname therefore receives the numeric IP on connection attempts and can fail even though bootstrap resolution succeeded. Preserve the configured hostname alongside the resolved address without another DNS lookup, retaining any IPv6 scope, and add a regression test with an unnamed resolver result.

This test can pass even if bootstrap resolution bypasses the injected resolver. The real cluster hostname resolves through JVM DNS, and the existing connection-time resolver can consume the two simulated failures before listTopics succeeds, satisfying both assertions. Use a bootstrap hostname that only the injected resolver can resolve, while retaining the real broker port, so reverting bootstrap injection makes this test fail.

Validate the port range before calling the resolver. Previously, `InetSocketAddress(host, port)` rejected an out-of-range port before attempting DNS. Now, if resolution throws `UnknownHostException`, this branch catches it and skips the address without checking its port. For example, `parseAndValidateAddresses(["bad.invalid:70000", "127.0.0.1:9092"], USE_ALL_DNS_IPS)` accepts the configuration when the first hostname cannot be resolved, instead of throwing `ConfigException`. Restore the range check before resolution, and add a regression test with an injected resolver that fails for the invalid-port entry and succeeds for the valid entry.

commit.message:
Route bootstrap DNS resolution through HostResolver

Bootstrap DNS resolution previously called InetAddress/InetSocketAddress
directly, bypassing HostResolver, the abstraction NetworkClient already
uses for post-bootstrap reconnection resolution to make DNS behavior
injectable in tests. This made the async bootstrap.resolve.timeout.ms path
untestable without real DNS infrastructure.

Route bootstrap resolution through HostResolver too, reusing the same
injection point already exposed by KafkaAdminClient#createInternal. The
default DNS lookup mode still resolves to a single address per host to
preserve existing behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Address Copilot review: preserve bootstrap hostname, tighten IT assertion

Resolving through an injected HostResolver can return an "unnamed"
InetAddress (e.g. from an IP literal), which previously replaced the
configured bootstrap hostname in the resulting InetSocketAddress. Since
Cluster.bootstrap() copies that into Node.host() and reconnection logic
re-resolves it later, this could key later lookups on the wrong value.
Re-attach the originally configured hostname (preserving IPv6 scope) without
an extra DNS lookup, and add a regression test.

Also tighten AsyncBootstrapResolutionTest: it previously used the real
cluster hostname, so it could pass even if bootstrap resolution bypassed
the injected resolver (the real hostname resolves via JVM DNS regardless).
Use an RFC 6761 .invalid hostname paired with the real broker's port
instead, so reverting the injection now makes the test fail for real
(verified locally).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Address Copilot review: validate port before resolving the host

In the default DNS lookup branch, resolution now happens before the port
range is checked. If resolution throws UnknownHostException, that catch
swallows the entry without ever validating its port, so e.g.
parseAndValidateAddresses(["bad.invalid:70000", "127.0.0.1:9092"], ...)
would silently accept the config instead of throwing ConfigException.

Restore the unconditional port range check before attempting resolution,
matching InetSocketAddress(host, port)'s own behavior, and add a regression
test with an injected resolver that fails for the invalid-port entry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
